comments.text: These are interesting but they are arrived at by very different yardsticks. The Spanish Moroccan border at Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera is in fact not the totality of the land border between the two countries, as Spain has two other exclaves on the south side of the Med, Ceuta and Melilla. So the total Spanish-Moroccan land border is in fact the sum of all three and quite a lot longer than 85metres. Also, counting in micro-states like The Vatican and Monaco is a bit pointless, I mean mosquitoes will have smaller wings than eagles and small countries will have shorter borders than bigger ones. The most impressive of the lot is the Botswana-Zambia border , which, given how actually huge the two countries are, and how much longer their total border lines with all the rest of their neighbours are, makes that 150m strip a winner in my books.
